axis_supply.supply_status: Critical deterioration - 90. leichte Division in Q1 1943 during Tunisia Campaign defensive operations (Mareth Line, January-March 1943). Supply situation severely degraded from Q4 1942: fuel critically low at 1.5 days (barely sufficient for local tactical movement), ammunition dangerously low at 3 days (severely rationed for defensive combat only), water 6L/man/day (50,520L total / 8,420 personnel, minimum survival level for Tunisia). Complete Allied air/naval supremacy strangling all supply lines from Tunis/Bizerte. Division severely weakened by attrition during retreat from El Alamein (Nov-Dec 1942). Commander Theodor Graf von Sponeck continuing command. Division manning Mareth Line defensive positions, awaiting Montgomery's Eighth Army assault. Personnel strength reduced 14.5% from Q4 1942 (9,847 to 8,420) due to combat losses, disease, and no replacements. Vehicle losses 16.4% (1,247 to 1,043). Supply bases: Tunis (350km north), Sfax (120km north), both under constant Allied air attack. Axis supply situation in Tunisia catastrophic - Allied interdiction of Mediterranean convoys, lack of fuel/ammunition/spare parts.

allied_supply.supply_status: Adequate for defensive operations after March 1943 reorganization. Initial shortages following Kasserine Pass addressed by replacement equipment and ammunition from Algerian ports. Primary constraint: extended supply lines (200+ km) from coastal ports via limited rail and road network.
